history.summary: CSV DUPLICATE FLAG: this row ('Ralang Monastery', Mangan) is almost certainly a DUPLICATE of CSV row 903 - there is NO Ralang Monastery in Mangan district. The real Ralang Monastery is at Ralang village, ~6-13 km from Ravangla in Namchi district (South Sikkim). Do not merge blindly: confirm row 903 covers this temple and deprecate this row, or keep with cross-reference. THIS IS A BUDDHIST MONASTERY (KAGYU), NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. The old gonpa (Karma Rabtenling) was founded in 1730 by Chogyal Gyurmed Namgyal after meeting the 12th Karmapa Changchub Dorje in Tibet (flag: some published accounts attribute this to the 9th Karmapa - verify); legend says the Karmapa blessed the site with rice grains tossed from Tsurphu, Tibet. The old monastery was rebuilt 1975-81; the New Ralang Monastery (Palchen Choeling Monastic Institute) was built in 1995 by the 12th Gyaltsab Rinpoche. The complex is noted for its rich collection of paintings and thangkas.

town_description: Ralang village lies a short drive from Ravangla in Namchi district, South Sikkim, in the Kanchenjunga foothills. Ravangla is a major Buddhist hub (Buddha Park/Tathagata Tsal, Ralang, Bon and Tibetan settlements); the area is ringed by tea gardens and forest with views of the Greater Himalaya.
tradition: Buddhism (Tibetan, Kagyu) - NOT a Hindu temple
